Notes: Module dependency rules checked by the CheckIncludes step of Scripts/Lint.py (Docs/Architecture.md section 3), and the path scopes of its banned-API, Python and JSON steps.

Modules: Layer and Includes encode the may-include column of the section 3 table. MaxLayer N allows every module of layer N or lower (the table's '<=N'). Layer-5 modules never list each other in Includes: same-layer edges between them exist only in Layer5Edges, where [X, Y] means Y may include X. Headers lists single headers of other modules a module may include. Project names in Includes (ShaderShared) allow that project's headers.

ThirdParty lists library names from the ThirdParty section, or Library:header for one header of a library. Public applies to public headers, Private to .cpp files and to headers in PrivateDirectories (which also includes everything in Public). GlobalThirdParty applies to every first-party file. 'System' is any header that is neither standard library, vendored nor first-party (OS and compiler headers); SystemHeaders is 'Private' (any private file of the module) or a list of module subdirectories.

Projects map paths to rules and are matched in order. Kind Engine files take the rules of their module (Engine/Source/Engine/<Module>/); FilesOutsideModules gives files at the project root the rules of a module. FlagsFrom names the project whose compile flags compile a file alone (header self-containment, clang-tidy).

PlatformDirectories.Notes: Platform-specific directories (Architecture Appendix A) and the host systems that compile them, as in Engine/premake5.lua. Files in a directory for another system are not compiled on this host.

GlobalThirdParty.Notes: glm is the math vocabulary of every module. Headers use only the forward declarations of nlohmann/json; typed reads go through Core/Json (the banned step enforces that).

Modules.Name: Core
Modules.Notes: spdlog appears in one public header, Log.h (section 3), so no other Core header leaks it into every module; Core's .cpp files and Private/ headers may use it.

Modules.Name: ImGui
Modules.Notes: NVRHI handles may appear in ImGui headers (section 3 rule 3); GLFW is needed by the GLFW glue (ImGui/ImGuiGlfwImplementation.cpp, section 2.2).

Modules.Name: App
Modules.Notes: vulkan.hpp is needed by the frame-boundary catch of vk::SystemError in App/FrameLoop.cpp (section 4.6).

SnapshotHeaders.Notes: Renderer/RenderSnapshot.h and Renderer/DebugDrawList.h, the only Renderer headers Scene may include, include nothing beyond Core, Asset, glm and the standard library, directly or transitively; in particular no NVRHI (section 3 rule 3). Transitively, the third-party headers that Core and Asset public headers may include are accepted.

Projects.Name: Engine
Projects.Notes: EnginePCH.h is included first by every Engine source file, Core's included, so it may only include what Core may.

Projects.Name: EditorCore
Projects.Notes: UI-free: every Engine module except ImGui, and no third-party headers of its own beyond the global ones (glm, nlohmann), except LuauAnalysis in the script type checker (section 3). The type checker may also include the Luau Ast/Common headers that the Analysis API is written in. EditorPCH.h is shared with Editor and follows the stricter EditorCore rules.

Projects.Name: Runtime
Projects.Notes: Engine except AssetPipeline, no Editor headers, ImGui only under #if !defined(ENGINE_DIST) (section 3).

Projects.Name: ShaderShared
Projects.Notes: Headers shared by C++ and Slang (section 8.4): only each other and the standard library. Compiled as C++ with the Engine flags.

Banned.Notes: Path scopes of the banned-API step. SimulationPathModules may not call CRT transcendental functions (section 4.12); SimulationPathExceptions lists files of those modules that do not affect simulated state. TryCatchFiles are the boundary files of section 4.6 (Scripting needs none: lua_pcall catches Luau errors inside the VM and bindings are exception-neutral). JsonAccessFiles may call nlohmann json at()/get<>(). AbiMacroFiles may #define the ABI-relevant configuration macros the step otherwise bans: only EnTT's configuration header (section 4.5).

Python.Notes: CodeStyle section 15. EntryPoints are the developer scripts: PascalCase file names ending with sys.exit(main()). Libraries use snake_case module names. ThirdPartyImports may import packages outside the standard library (the MCP bridge runs in its own virtual environment).

Json.Notes: Authored formats of section 6 plus every .json file. Fixtures under Tests/Data are exercised by the unit tests, some deliberately malformed.
